title: The Battle Game Trap
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Kogoro Mouri (absent this episode), Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention -- Sonoko and Conan perform the deduction/reenactment on-screen but are structural cast, not case-specific figures. Jodie Saintemillion is kept as a full person node because she is a named suspect central to this case's opportunity/alibi puzzle (and the episode's coda hints at her undercover identity), unlike the omitted recurring quartet. The old wiki-derived case file (cases/ep226-227_the_battle_game_trap.json) got the culprit (Shimizu Takayasu) and rough motive direction right, but its motive_type ('financially burdened the culprit's sister who worked to pay it off') undersells the actual transcript stakes -- the sister was going blind from vitamin-A-deficiency malnutrition after starving herself for a month to pay Bito's gambling debts, and Shimizu's crime followed directly from losing a wagered 'final game' in which Bito promised to leave her alone if beaten fairly. The old file also collapsed everything into generic 'knows' edges and a single vague murder event, omitted Jodie, Dejima, and Emori's individual backstories/motives entirely, and did not capture the character-swap/forced-draw mechanic, the coin-count evidence, or the ash-tray-sourced weapon materials that explain why the culprit's own signature gum brand didn't match the weapon. No discrepancy in murderer identity was found -- Shimizu Takayasu is confirmed as the culprit by the transcript as well. case_type: murder.

objects.name: Poisoned needle hidden inside a cigarette, packaged with chewing gum and a gum wrapper

attrs.lethality: as little as 0.5-1 mg can be fatal; if ingested it works slowly through the bloodstream, but direct injection causes near-instant paralysis and death
attrs.construction: a needle hidden inside a cigarette, held together with chewing gum, the whole assembly stuck to a gum wrapper so it could be dropped, stepped on, and picked back up without leaving the discarder's own fingerprints
attrs.disposal_method: planted on the arcade floor near Bito's seat under cover of retrieving a dropped lighter; later stuck to the sole of Dejima's shoe when he stepped on it, producing a faint metal-scratching sound as he walked afterward
attrs.materials_origin: cigarette, gum, and wrapper scavenged from a public ashtray rather than being Shimizu's own brand, so nothing could be brand- or fingerprint-matched back to him directly

objects.name: "Great Fighter Spirit" virtual-reality fighting game console (Beika Caesar side, Bito's machine)

attrs.mechanism: players wear headgear and are strapped in with a chest guard; force-feedback makes the player's own body flinch and move when their character is hit, simulating real combat
attrs.flaw_exploited: the game displays no on-screen hit-point gauge, so spectators can only judge who's winning by watching the players' bodies -- making it possible to disguise which physical person is really controlling which character
attrs.match_result: ended in a Draw rather than a clean win for Beika Caesar

objects.name: Shimizu's own signature lucky chewing gum

attrs.reputation: Shimizu's well-known pre-match good-luck habit, prominent enough to have been featured in a gaming magazine
attrs.role_in_crime: used as a decoy -- by visibly chewing his own signature gum in front of the police right after the murder, his habitual gum-chewing looked unrelated to the different-brand gum used to disguise the murder weapon

clues.desc: The match ended in a Draw instead of a clean win for Beika Caesar (Bito's character), even though Haido Lucas (Shimizu's character) was on the verge of being knocked out and time was nearly up -- a real winning blow would have triggered a 'You Lose' screen on Bito's own console, exposing that he wasn't the one actually playing. The culprit deliberately withheld the finishing hit to avoid that reveal.

Bito's arcade machine's coin box held one 100-yen coin more than the number of legitimate insertions (Bito's own coin, plus the one used in the police's later reenactment) -- proving a third, uncounted-for person inserted a coin into that specific machine during the murder window, and that coin carries Shimizu's fingerprints.

The cigarette and gum used to wrap the murder weapon were a different brand from Shimizu's own well-known signature lucky gum -- not proof of innocence, but evidence he deliberately used items scavenged from a public ashtray so the weapon couldn't be brand- or fingerprint-matched to him, while continuing to chew his own real gum in front of the police to make his habit look unrelated to the crime.
